assessment.title: HVAC Knowledge Assessment
assessment.description: A knowledge assessment of HVAC safety, electrical, refrigeration, equipment, and diagnostics. Scores are not a license or certification.

version.instructions: Answer each question to the best of your knowledge. You can go back and change answers before submitting. This is a knowledge assessment, not a license or certification.

categories.name: Safety, Tools & Work Practices
categories.description: Jobsite safety, refrigerant handling, tools, and professional work practices.

questions.prompt: Before servicing a rooftop unit, what is the safest first action for the electrical supply?
questions.explanation: De-energize the circuit, apply lockout/tagout, and verify the absence of voltage with a meter before contacting conductors or components.

choices.body: Lock out the disconnect and verify the circuit is de-energized with a meter
Open the access panel and start tracing wires while the unit is still powered
Remove the thermostat batteries so the unit cannot call
Close the gas valve and assume the electrical circuit is also isolated

questions.prompt: Why must refrigerants be recovered instead of vented when a system is opened for repair?
questions.explanation: Venting most refrigerants is prohibited. Recovery protects the environment and is required before opening the sealed refrigerant circuit.

choices.body: Releasing refrigerant to the atmosphere is prohibited; it must be recovered into approved cylinders
Venting is faster and is acceptable if the charge is small
Refrigerant can be dumped into the condensate drain if it is mixed with water
Only flammable refrigerants need to be recovered

questions.prompt: What personal protective equipment is most important when cutting sheet metal or grinding?
questions.explanation: Eye and face protection prevent common, serious injuries from metal fragments. Hearing and hand protection may also be needed, but eyes are the first priority for cutting and grinding.

choices.body: Safety glasses or a face shield rated for impact
A cotton shop rag tied over the face
Sunscreen and a hat only
Leather welding sleeves without eye protection

questions.prompt: When using a portable ladder, which practice is safest?
questions.explanation: Maintain three points of contact and set the ladder on stable footing. Overreaching and standing on the top cap are common causes of falls.

choices.body: Keep three points of contact and do not stand on the top cap or top step
Lean the ladder on a gutter and stand on the top cap to reach farther
Have a coworker bounce the base to walk the ladder closer to the work
Place the ladder on a wet coil box lid to gain height

questions.prompt: Where should a technician look first for hazard information about a chemical used on the job?
questions.explanation: The Safety Data Sheet (SDS) is the standard source for hazards, PPE, first aid, and spill response.

choices.body: The Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for that product
The equipment installation sticker only
A coworker’s memory of a similar product
The customer’s homeowner warranty packet

questions.prompt: A belt-driven blower must be inspected. What should be done before removing the belt guard?
questions.explanation: Moving belts and pulleys are pinch-point hazards. Lock out power and verify the blower cannot start before removing guards.

choices.body: Lock out power and verify the blower cannot start
Remove the guard quickly while the blower coasts to a stop
Hold the belt with a rag while the motor is still energized
Bypass the door switch so the blower can be observed running without the guard

questions.prompt: Why is fall protection a concern on a typical residential or light-commercial rooftop?
questions.explanation: Unprotected roof edges, wet surfaces, and skylights create fall hazards. Plan access, stay away from edges, and use required fall protection.

choices.body: Unprotected roof edges, wet surfaces, and skylights can cause serious falls
Rooftop work is exempt from fall awareness because units are low
Fall protection is only needed if the unit is running
A tool belt is sufficient fall protection

questions.prompt: A system must be pressure-tested after a repair. Which gas is the appropriate choice for a dry pressure test?
questions.explanation: Dry nitrogen, regulated to a safe test pressure, is the standard pressure-test gas. Oxygen, compressed air with moisture, and unregulated cylinder pressure are unsafe or contaminating.

choices.body: Dry nitrogen supplied through a regulator set to a safe test pressure
Oxygen from a cutting torch cylinder to raise pressure faster
Unregulated nitrogen straight from the cylinder valve
Acetylene because it is lighter than air and finds leaks quickly

questions.prompt: When recovering refrigerant, why must a recovery cylinder not be filled to the top?
questions.explanation: Liquid refrigerant expands with temperature. Overfilling can rupture a cylinder. Stay within the cylinder’s rated fill limit, commonly about 80% by volume.

choices.body: Leaving vapor headspace prevents hydrostatic rupture as temperature rises
A completely full cylinder recovers refrigerant faster
Cylinders are designed to be liquid-packed with no vapor space
Overfilling is acceptable if the cylinder is stored in the shade

questions.prompt: Why is a nitrogen purge used while brazing refrigerant piping?
questions.explanation: Flowing dry nitrogen during brazing displaces oxygen and reduces copper oxide scale inside the pipe, protecting the compressor and metering device.

choices.body: It reduces internal oxidation (scale) that can contaminate the system
It increases joint temperature so the braze flows more easily
It replaces the need for a later leak test
It is used only to make the flame burn quieter

questions.prompt: A disconnect is open, but the technician has not yet verified voltage. What should be done next?
questions.explanation: An open handle does not guarantee isolation. Test the meter on a known live source, check the load side, then re-check the meter. Never trust the handle alone.

choices.body: Verify the absence of voltage with a meter using a known-live test of the meter
Begin work because an open disconnect is always de-energized
Remove the thermostat only; that isolates line voltage
Touch the conductor with the back of the hand to confirm it is dead

questions.prompt: How should refrigerant cylinders be stored on a service truck?
questions.explanation: Store cylinders upright, secured against tipping, away from heat sources, and with valves protected. Horizontal storage of liquid-service cylinders and unsecured loads are unsafe.

choices.body: Upright, secured, valve-protected, and away from heat sources
On their sides under the seat so they stay cool
Loose in the bed so they can be unloaded quickly
Inside the occupied cab with the valves open to equalize pressure

questions.prompt: A technician working a hot attic begins to feel dizzy and nauseated. What is the safest immediate action?
questions.explanation: Heat illness can escalate quickly. Stop work, move to a cooler area, hydrate, and get help. Continuing work or taking salt tablets without evaluation is unsafe.

choices.body: Stop work, move to a cooler area, and get assistance
Finish the brazing job first so the system is not left open
Drink an energy drink and continue at a faster pace to finish sooner
Take extra salt tablets and remain in the attic until the job is done

questions.prompt: When brazing near combustible building materials, which control is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: A fire watch, shielding, and a suitable extinguisher are required when open flame is used near combustibles. Water on electrical equipment or leaving the site immediately after the last braze is not adequate.

choices.body: Shield combustibles, keep an extinguisher ready, and watch the area after the flame is out
Spray water into the electrical control box to pre-wet it
Leave as soon as the last joint is made; residual heat is never a risk
Increase oxygen flow so the braze is finished before materials can ignite

questions.prompt: Why must gauges and hoses be rated for the refrigerant and pressure of the system being serviced?
questions.explanation: High-pressure refrigerants such as R-410A can exceed the rating of older R-22 gauges and hoses, creating a rupture and injury hazard.

choices.body: Underrated gauges or hoses can fail under the system’s operating or standing pressure
Color-matched hoses recover refrigerant faster regardless of rating
Any manifold can be used if the valves are opened slowly
Low-pressure gauges are preferred because they are more accurate at high pressure

questions.prompt: A crawlspace has a fuel-fired appliance and limited ventilation. What hazard should the technician consider before extended work?
questions.explanation: Confined or poorly ventilated spaces can accumulate combustion gases, refrigerant, or oxygen-deficient air. Assess atmosphere, ventilation, and egress before extended work.

choices.body: Possible oxygen deficiency or accumulation of combustion products or refrigerant
Crawlspaces are always safe if a flashlight works
Only noise exposure is a concern in crawlspaces
Ventilation is unnecessary if the technician works quickly

questions.prompt: What is the correct action if a refrigerant cylinder’s relief device is damaged or the cylinder is visibly bulging?
questions.explanation: A compromised cylinder is a pressure vessel failure risk. Do not use it. Isolate it, keep heat away, and follow supplier/hazmat procedures.

choices.body: Do not use it; isolate it from heat and follow the supplier’s emergency guidance
Hammer the valve to reseat the relief device
Fill it completely so liquid cushions the damaged relief
Warm it with a torch to restore roundness, then continue service

questions.prompt: Before using a torch, which check is part of safe setup?
questions.explanation: Inspect hoses, connections, reverse-flow protection, and regulator condition. Light with an approved striker, not a cigarette lighter in an uncontrolled way, and never use oil on oxygen equipment.

choices.body: Inspect hoses, fittings, and regulators for damage and leaks
Crack the oxygen valve and check for leaks with oil-coated hands
Light the torch with a gasoline-soaked rag for a hotter start
Disable flashback arrestors because they slow gas flow

questions.prompt: A technician must work on a unit that can be started from a thermostat, a building control, and a service disconnect. What is the key lockout principle?
questions.explanation: All energy sources and start paths that can energize the equipment must be isolated and verified. Locking only the thermostat does not control line voltage.

choices.body: Isolate and verify every energy source that can start or energize the equipment
Lock the thermostat cover; line voltage cannot start the equipment without a call
Tag the unit only; physical locks are optional on residential equipment
Remove one fuse and leave the other leg hot for lighting

questions.prompt: A packaged rooftop unit is fed by three-phase power, has a 24-volt control circuit, and a gas supply. What is the safest isolation sequence before opening the blower section?
questions.explanation: Control power, line voltage, and fuel are separate energy sources. Shut down, lock and tag the electrical disconnect, verify absence of voltage, and isolate fuel if work could release gas or if burners could fire. Do not rely on a thermostat off switch.

choices.body: De-energize and lock the electrical disconnect, verify no voltage, and isolate fuel if burner operation is possible
Turn the thermostat to OFF and immediately remove the blower access panel
Close the gas valve only; electricity cannot run a gas-pack blower
Pull the condensate float switch wire so the unit cannot call for heat

questions.prompt: When working with a mildly flammable (A2L) refrigerant, which practice is appropriate?
questions.explanation: A2L refrigerants require ignition-source control, good ventilation, leak checking, and manufacturer/safe-handling procedures. They are not treated as nonflammable R-410A look-alikes, and they must not be vented.

choices.body: Control ignition sources, ventilate the work area, and follow the equipment and refrigerant handling procedures
Treat A2L refrigerants exactly like nonflammable R-410A with no extra controls
Vent a small A2L charge outdoors to speed the repair
Use an open-flame leak detector as the primary method because the dye is hard to see

questions.prompt: A nitrogen cylinder is being used for brazing purge and pressure testing. Which setup is required?
questions.explanation: Cylinder pressure must be reduced with a regulator. A relief or downstream pressure control appropriate to the application is required. Never connect an unregulated cylinder to a system or braze purge line.

choices.body: A pressure regulator (and appropriate relief) so downstream pressure stays within a safe range
A full-open cylinder valve with no regulator so flow is unrestricted
A torch oxygen regulator because any regulator body will work on nitrogen
A cap on the unused hose instead of a regulator

questions.prompt: A system contains an unknown refrigerant and oil mix. What should the technician do before recovery and repair?
questions.explanation: Identify the refrigerant (and consider oil compatibility) before recovery so the correct recovery equipment, cylinder, and procedures are used. Mixing refrigerants and dumping into an assumed cylinder contaminates the supply and can create unsafe pressures.

choices.body: Identify the refrigerant and use compatible recovery equipment and a dedicated cylinder
Recover it into an R-22 cylinder because that is the most common leftover gas
Vent the unknown mix and recharge with the refrigerant the nameplate lists
Add a can of the nameplate refrigerant to dilute whatever is in the system

questions.prompt: During recovery, the technician notices the recovery cylinder is frosting heavily and pressure is rising toward the cylinder’s rating. What is the safest next step?
questions.explanation: Stop and reassess. Overfill, mixing, a blocked path, or pumping liquid against a closed valve can overpressurize a cylinder. Do not continue filling, do not heat the cylinder with a torch, and do not bypass relief devices.

choices.body: Stop recovery, check fill level and hose routing, and move to a proper empty cylinder if needed
Keep recovering; frost means the cylinder still has plenty of capacity
Heat the cylinder with a torch so pressure equalizes faster
Disable the recovery machine’s high-pressure cutout to finish the job

categories.name: Electrical Fundamentals
categories.description: HVAC electrical theory, controls, and safe electrical troubleshooting.

questions.prompt: In simple terms, what does voltage represent in a circuit?
questions.explanation: Voltage is electrical pressure that pushes current through a resistance. Current is flow; resistance opposes flow; power is the rate of energy use.

choices.body: Electrical pressure that causes current to flow
The flow of electrons through a conductor
Opposition to current flow
The amount of heat a motor can reject

questions.prompt: When should a continuity test be performed?
questions.explanation: Continuity and resistance checks are made on a de-energized circuit. Measuring ohms on a live circuit can damage the meter and give false readings.

choices.body: On a de-energized circuit after power is verified off
While the circuit is at full line voltage so the reading is realistic
Only across the utility transformer primary
In parallel with a running compressor

questions.prompt: What is the primary job of a contactor in an outdoor condensing unit?
questions.explanation: A contactor is a switch that uses a control-voltage coil to connect and disconnect line-voltage loads such as the compressor and condenser fan.

choices.body: Switch line-voltage power to loads when the control coil is energized
Step 240 volts down to 24 volts
Store extra current for compressor start
Protect the circuit from ground faults like a GFCI

questions.prompt: What does a typical HVAC control transformer do?
questions.explanation: The control transformer steps line voltage down to a safer, lower control voltage, commonly 24 volts AC, for thermostats and relays.

choices.body: Reduce line voltage to a lower control voltage
Increase 24 volts to 240 volts for the compressor
Convert refrigerant pressure into a voltage signal
Store energy for the compressor start winding

questions.prompt: Why does HVAC equipment include an equipment grounding path?
questions.explanation: An equipment grounding conductor provides a low-impedance path for fault current so overcurrent devices can open and exposed metal is less likely to remain energized.

choices.body: To give fault current a path that helps clear the fault and reduce shock hazard
To carry normal operating current to the compressor
To increase the voltage available at the motors
To keep the thermostat display backlit

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a fuse or circuit breaker feeding an air conditioner?
questions.explanation: Overcurrent devices protect conductors and equipment from overload and short-circuit current. They are not a substitute for disconnecting means during service.

choices.body: Protect the circuit from overcurrent
Raise voltage if the utility supply sags
Store extra current for starting
Convert single-phase power to three-phase power

questions.prompt: A residential split system typically uses which combination of voltages?
questions.explanation: Line-voltage loads commonly operate at 120/240 volts, while thermostats and many control devices use 24 volts.

choices.body: Line voltage for motors and 24-volt control for the thermostat circuit
480-volt controls and 24-volt compressors
Battery-only power for the outdoor unit
Line voltage on the thermostat R and C terminals as the normal design

questions.prompt: A 24-volt control circuit has a 40-ohm coil. Approximately how much current does the coil draw?
questions.explanation: Ohm’s law: I = V / R = 24 / 40 = 0.6 A. This is typical of a small control load.

choices.body: 0.6 ampere
6 amperes
0.06 milliampere
40 amperes

questions.prompt: How should a clamp-on ammeter be used to measure current to a compressor?
questions.explanation: Clamp around a single current-carrying conductor. Clamping the entire cable (hot and neutral/return together) cancels the magnetic field and reads near zero.

choices.body: Clamp around one current-carrying conductor only
Clamp around the entire power cable including all conductors
Clamp around the refrigerant suction line
Clamp around the grounding conductor only

questions.prompt: A run capacitor in a single-phase compressor circuit is primarily used to:
questions.explanation: The run capacitor provides a phase-shifted current to the start (auxiliary) winding while the motor runs, improving torque and efficiency.

choices.body: Provide a phase shift for the auxiliary winding during running
Increase line voltage to 480 volts
Store refrigerant during the off cycle
Ground the compressor shell during a fault

questions.prompt: A technician measures 24 volts at the transformer secondary but 0 volts at thermostat R. What is the most logical early check?
questions.explanation: Power leaves the transformer through a fuse, wiring, and sometimes a door or float switch. An open in that path explains voltage at the transformer and none at R. Replacing the compressor first is not logical.

choices.body: Look for an open fuse, disconnected wire, or open safety in the R circuit
Replace the compressor because it is the largest load
Add refrigerant until 24 volts appears at the thermostat
Reverse the transformer primary taps to boost control voltage

questions.prompt: Why can a voltage reading from a high-impedance meter on an open conductor be misleading?
questions.explanation: High-impedance meters can show phantom or ghost voltage from capacitive coupling. A low-impedance meter or a known load helps distinguish a real source from a ghost reading.

choices.body: The meter may display phantom voltage that cannot supply useful current
High-impedance meters never display voltage on open wires
Any displayed voltage always means a solid utility feed
Phantom voltage only occurs on fiber-optic cables

questions.prompt: A thermostat is calling for cooling. There is 24 volts from Y to C at the outdoor unit, but the contactor does not pull in. What should be checked next?
questions.explanation: Control voltage is present, so the next checks are the contactor coil path, coil resistance, and whether the coil is open or mechanically jammed—not immediately the compressor windings.

choices.body: Contactor coil circuit continuity and whether the coil is open or the armature is jammed
Indoor blower wheel balance only
The condensate drain slope
The filter-drier for a temperature drop, before checking the coil

questions.prompt: What is a practical difference between a relay and a contactor in HVAC equipment?
questions.explanation: Contactors are built to switch higher-current line-voltage loads such as compressors. Relays typically switch lighter control or small loads. Both are electrically operated switches.

choices.body: Contactors are typically used for higher-current line-voltage loads
Relays can switch unlimited compressor current; contactors cannot
Contactors only work on DC; relays only work on AC
There is no current or construction difference; the names are random

questions.prompt: A technician needs to know if a fuse is open. The circuit is de-energized. Which method is appropriate?
questions.explanation: With power off and the fuse isolated as required, continuity or resistance across the fuse identifies an open. Measuring ohms on an energized fuse is the wrong tool use.

choices.body: Measure continuity or resistance across the de-energized fuse
Measure resistance across the fuse while the circuit is live
Look for refrigerant oil on the fuse body
Clamp an ammeter around the fuse while power is off and expect full load current

questions.prompt: Why are many 24-volt safety devices wired in series with the control circuit?
questions.explanation: Series safeties (float switch, limit, rollout, pressure switch) open the control path so the equipment stops when any one safety opens. Parallel wiring would allow the unit to keep running with a safety open.

choices.body: Any one open safety can interrupt the control path and stop the equipment
Series wiring increases control voltage at the load
It allows the unit to ignore a single open safety
It converts 24 volts to line voltage

questions.prompt: A call for cooling requires the indoor blower and the outdoor unit. On a typical 24-volt thermostat, which terminals are commonly involved?
questions.explanation: R is power, Y is cooling, G is fan, C is common. W is heating. Knowing the call path is basic electrical troubleshooting.

choices.body: R, Y, and G (and C for common)
W only
The compressor run capacitor terminals only
The gas valve solenoid terminals only

questions.prompt: Voltage at a motor is 240 volts with no load but sags significantly when the compressor tries to start. What does this suggest?
questions.explanation: Excessive voltage drop under load points to supply, wiring, connections, or an undersized circuit—not a need to add refrigerant. Investigate the electrical path before condemning the compressor.

choices.body: High resistance or an inadequate supply path in the power circuit
The system is overcharged and must be recovered immediately
The thermostat anticipator is set too high
The condensate trap is dry

questions.prompt: An ECM indoor blower is not running. Line voltage is present at the module. What is a logical next check before replacing the motor?
questions.explanation: Many ECM blowers need a control signal (and often 24 volts) in addition to line voltage. Confirm calls, harness, and control voltage before replacing the motor.

choices.body: Confirm the control signal/harness and any required 24-volt supply to the module
Add a start capacitor across the ECM as if it were a PSC motor
Jump line voltage directly to the communication pins
Reverse the equipment grounding conductor and a power leg

questions.prompt: A dual-run capacitor is labeled 35+5 µF. The compressor will not start; the condenser fan runs. Which check is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The larger value typically serves the compressor and the smaller the fan. If the fan runs, the fan section and one winding path may be intact. Measure capacitance (after safe discharge) of the compressor section and check start/run windings rather than replacing the transformer first.

choices.body: Safely discharge the capacitor and measure the compressor (HERM) microfarad section
Replace the control transformer because 24 volts cannot start a compressor
Increase the refrigerant charge to raise starting torque
Bypass the outdoor fan so all current goes to the compressor

questions.prompt: A dual-voltage three-phase motor can be connected for 230 or 460 volts. What must the technician verify before applying power after a motor replacement?
questions.explanation: Taps and jumper configuration must match the supply voltage. A 230-volt connection on 460 volts can destroy the motor; a 460-volt connection on 230 volts will not develop proper torque.

choices.body: The winding tap/jumper configuration matches the available supply voltage
That all three windings are connected in series regardless of supply voltage
That the equipment grounding conductor is left disconnected to avoid circulating current
That two phases are swapped until the nameplate voltage appears on a single winding

questions.prompt: A technician reads about 120 volts from each outdoor unit leg to ground on a 240-volt single-phase circuit, but 0 volts across the two legs at the contactor load side while the coil is pulled in. What is the most likely explanation?
questions.explanation: Each leg to ground can read ~120 volts even if the contactor is not passing both legs to the load, or if the meter is reading on the line side. 0 volts across the two load terminals with the coil pulled in suggests the contacts are not closing a complete 240-volt path. Do not assume the compressor is shorted without confirming voltage at the compressor terminals.

choices.body: The load-side 240-volt path is open, such as failed contactor contacts
The compressor is definitely shorted to ground
The control transformer secondary is open
The indoor thermostat C wire is missing

questions.prompt: An outdoor unit has a communicating indoor controller. There is line voltage at the outdoor terminals, but the unit never starts. What is a sound early diagnostic step?
questions.explanation: Communicating systems need intact communication wiring, correct polarity/configuration, and often a control module handshake—not just line voltage. Verify communication wiring and status codes before replacing the compressor.

choices.body: Check communication wiring, configuration, and module status indications
Add a conventional 24-volt Y jump at the outdoor contactor and leave it permanently
Charge the system to nameplate weight before any electrical diagnosis
Remove the equipment ground so communication noise decreases

questions.prompt: A compressor hums and trips the breaker in a few seconds. Supply voltage is stable, and the contactor stays pulled in until the breaker opens. What should be evaluated before condemning the compressor as a grounded winding?
questions.explanation: Locked-rotor current from a failed start component, a mechanical lock, or a winding issue can all trip a breaker. Discharge and check capacitors, confirm voltage at the terminals during the attempt, and check winding resistances to ground and between terminals. Jumping the breaker or adding refrigerant is not a diagnosis.

choices.body: Starting components, applied voltage at the compressor terminals, and winding resistance to ground
Install a larger breaker so the compressor can start
Add refrigerant to cushion the pistons
Remove the overload and jump it out of the circuit permanently

categories.name: HVAC & Refrigeration Fundamentals
categories.description: Refrigeration cycle, heat transfer, airflow, and charging fundamentals.

questions.prompt: In the vapor-compression cycle, where does the refrigerant absorb heat from the conditioned space?
questions.explanation: The evaporator is where liquid/vapor refrigerant absorbs heat and vaporizes at low pressure.

choices.body: The evaporator
The condenser
The compressor crankcase heater
The liquid-line filter-drier only

questions.prompt: Where does the refrigeration cycle reject heat?
questions.explanation: The condenser rejects heat as high-pressure vapor desuperheats, condenses, and usually subcools.

choices.body: The condenser
The evaporator coil only
The indoor return-air filter
The thermostat

questions.prompt: What is the compressor’s primary function in the refrigeration cycle?
questions.explanation: The compressor raises refrigerant vapor pressure (and temperature) so heat can be rejected in the condenser, and it moves refrigerant through the circuit.

choices.body: To raise the pressure of refrigerant vapor and circulate it through the system
To convert liquid refrigerant into oil
To drop liquid pressure like a metering device
To dry the air by absorbing moisture into the crankcase

questions.prompt: What is the function of a metering device such as a TXV or piston?
questions.explanation: The metering device creates the pressure drop between high-side liquid and the low-side evaporator.

choices.body: To reduce liquid refrigerant pressure entering the evaporator
To increase suction pressure above condensing pressure
To generate 24-volt control power
To store extra refrigerant during the winter

questions.prompt: What is superheat?
questions.explanation: Superheat is how many degrees a vapor is above its saturation temperature at that pressure. It helps confirm that vapor, not liquid, is returning to the compressor.

choices.body: The temperature of vapor above the saturation temperature at that pressure
The temperature of liquid below saturation at that pressure
The temperature difference between supply and outdoor air only
The current draw of the compressor in amperes

questions.prompt: What is subcooling?
questions.explanation: Subcooling is how many degrees a liquid is below its saturation temperature at that pressure. It helps confirm a full liquid column to the metering device.

choices.body: The temperature of liquid below the saturation temperature at that pressure
The temperature of vapor above saturation at that pressure
The amount of ice on the suction line
The thermostat heating anticipator setting

questions.prompt: What is a liquid-line filter-drier intended to do?
questions.explanation: A filter-drier removes moisture, acid, and particles that can damage the metering device and compressor.

choices.body: Trap moisture, acid, and debris in the liquid refrigerant stream
Increase compressor displacement
Replace the need for a vacuum after a repair
Raise evaporator pressure to condensing pressure

questions.prompt: A technician uses a pressure-temperature chart at the evaporator. What is being determined?
questions.explanation: Saturated temperature at the measured pressure is read from the P-T relationship so superheat or subcooling can be calculated from an actual thermometer reading.

choices.body: The saturation temperature that corresponds to the measured pressure
The exact outdoor dry-bulb temperature
The blower motor horsepower
The age of the compressor oil

questions.prompt: Compared with older R-22 air-conditioning systems, R-410A typically operates at:
questions.explanation: R-410A operating pressures are substantially higher than R-22. Service tools must be rated accordingly.

choices.body: Higher pressures
Much lower pressures in every mode
Identical pressures, which is why gauges are interchangeable without rating checks
A vacuum on the high side during normal cooling

questions.prompt: Why must POE oil be handled carefully during service?
questions.explanation: Polyolester oil is hygroscopic: it absorbs moisture from air, which can lead to acid and system damage. Minimize open time and keep containers sealed.

choices.body: It readily absorbs moisture from air
It never mixes with HFC refrigerants
It is a metallic solid at room temperature
It eliminates the need for a filter-drier

questions.prompt: Why is a deep vacuum pulled after a system is opened?
questions.explanation: Vacuum removes air and moisture (noncondensables and water vapor) that raise head pressure, freeze at the metering device, and form acid.

choices.body: To remove air and moisture before charging
To add extra oil capacity
To test the thermostat calibration
To increase the nameplate SEER rating

questions.prompt: Sensible heat is heat that:
questions.explanation: Sensible heat changes temperature that a thermometer can read. Latent heat changes state (moisture) without changing dry-bulb temperature the same way.

choices.body: Changes a substance’s temperature
Only changes a substance’s state, never its temperature
Is produced only by electric heaters
Cannot be measured with a thermometer in air

questions.prompt: A common starting airflow target for comfort cooling is about 400 cfm per ton. How should a technician treat this number?
questions.explanation: 400 cfm/ton is a common starting point, not a law. Actual airflow must match the equipment design, static capability, and application (humidity, heat pumps, furnaces).

choices.body: As a common starting point that still must be verified against the equipment and application
As a mandatory value for every heat pump and furnace regardless of design
As the outdoor fan airflow, not the indoor blower
As a refrigerant charging chart substitute

questions.prompt: What does external static pressure indicate about a ducted system?
questions.explanation: External static pressure is the resistance the blower sees from filters, coils, and ducts. High static reduces airflow.

choices.body: The airflow resistance the indoor blower is working against
The refrigerant condensing pressure
The gas manifold pressure
The thermostat droop in degrees

questions.prompt: In heat pump heating mode, the indoor coil acts as the:
questions.explanation: The reversing valve directs discharge vapor to the indoor coil so it condenses and rejects heat to the space. The indoor coil is the condenser in heating.

choices.body: Condenser
Only a metering device
Compressor
Crankcase heater

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of outdoor-coil defrost on an air-source heat pump?
questions.explanation: Frost on the outdoor coil blocks airflow and heat transfer. Defrost temporarily puts the unit into a cooling-like refrigerant flow so the outdoor coil can melt frost.

choices.body: To melt frost that blocks outdoor-coil airflow and heat transfer
To freeze the indoor coil on purpose for humidity control
To recover refrigerant into a cylinder
To calibrate the thermostat clock

questions.prompt: On a TXV system, which charging approach is commonly used once airflow is confirmed?
questions.explanation: TXV systems are commonly charged by subcooling (per manufacturer data). Fixed-orifice systems are commonly approached with superheat. Always follow the equipment charging method.

choices.body: Charge to the manufacturer’s target subcooling
Charge only until suction pressure equals liquid pressure
Charge by adding refrigerant until the compressor is silent
Charge by frost line to the compressor

questions.prompt: A temperature drop across a liquid-line filter-drier during steady cooling operation most nearly suggests:
questions.explanation: A restriction causes a pressure drop and flashing, which shows up as a temperature drop across the drier. It does not prove a bad compressor by itself.

choices.body: A possible restriction in the drier
That the drier is working normally by creating a large temperature drop
That the indoor filter is dirty
That the thermostat is miswired

questions.prompt: Latent cooling capacity is associated with:
questions.explanation: Latent capacity is moisture removal (dehumidification). Sensible capacity is dry-bulb temperature reduction.

choices.body: Removing moisture from the air
Raising dry-bulb temperature without changing moisture
The compressor’s locked-rotor amperes
The gas valve opening time

questions.prompt: A cooling system with a TXV shows high superheat and high subcooling after airflow is confirmed normal. Which problem is most consistent with those two readings together?
questions.explanation: High subcooling means liquid is backing up in the condenser; high superheat means the evaporator is starved. That combination points to a restriction between the condenser outlet and the TXV inlet (often a drier or liquid-line restriction), not a simple undercharge (which usually lowers subcooling).

choices.body: A restriction in the liquid line or filter-drier
A simple undercharge with no restriction
A dirty evaporator filter as the only cause
An overcharge with a wide-open metering device as the only cause

questions.prompt: A cooling system shows low superheat and low subcooling after indoor airflow has been verified. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.explanation: That pair of readings is not a single-part verdict. Low superheat can mean overfeeding; low subcooling can mean little liquid is stored in the condenser. Re-check probes and gauges first, then evaluate metering-device feed and charge together instead of replacing the compressor or adding refrigerant blindly.

choices.body: Re-verify gauge and temperature measurements, then evaluate metering-device feed and charge together
Replace the compressor immediately because those two readings always mean a failed compressor
Add several pounds of refrigerant without measuring because low subcooling always means undercharge only
Bypass the TXV with a piston as the first step

questions.prompt: Noncondensable gas is suspected in a recently repaired system. Which operating clue is most consistent, after confirming condenser airflow is good?
questions.explanation: Air or nitrogen left in the system raises condensing pressure and can make subcooling appear abnormal. Recovery, evacuation, and recharge are required—not adding more refrigerant to mask high head.

choices.body: Abnormally high head pressure for the outdoor conditions
Abnormally low head pressure with a cold condenser
A frozen condensate switch
A thermostat that will not display temperature

questions.prompt: A zeotropic blended refrigerant has noticeable temperature glide. What should the technician remember when reading a P-T relationship?
questions.explanation: Glide means bubble and dew temperatures differ. Superheat and subcooling must use the correct ends of the P-T data (dew for vapor, bubble for liquid) per the refrigerant’s data—not a single old single-compound habit.

choices.body: Use the correct dew or bubble value from the refrigerant data, not a single old R-22 habit
Ignore P-T data and charge only until the sight glass looks busy
Treat glide as proof the blend has fractionated and must be vented
Average the high-side and low-side pressures and use that as saturation for both coils

questions.prompt: A TXV is hunting (suction pressure swinging). Airflow and charge look reasonable. What is a logical next inspection?
questions.explanation: TXV hunting can come from an oversized valve, a poorly mounted or uninsulated sensing bulb, a blocked equalizer, or unstable load. Inspect bulb mounting/location/insulation and equalizer piping before replacing the compressor.

choices.body: Sensing-bulb mounting, insulation, and equalizer line condition
Replace the indoor thermostat first because hunting is a clock problem
Remove the filter-drier permanently to increase liquid velocity
Jump the high-pressure switch so the valve can stabilize

categories.name: Equipment, Components & Installation
categories.description: Equipment components, installation practices, and setup.

questions.prompt: Where is a disposable air filter typically installed on a ducted residential system?
questions.explanation: The filter is placed in the return path ahead of the blower and coil so it protects equipment and the coil from dirt.

choices.body: In the return-air path before the blower and indoor coil
On the compressor discharge line
Inside the thermostat subbase
On the outdoor fan motor shaft

questions.prompt: Why does an indoor condensate drain need slope and a trap where the equipment design requires one?
questions.explanation: Condensate must flow away by gravity, and a trap on negative-pressure drain pans prevents air from being pulled through the drain instead of water leaving the pan.

choices.body: To let water leave the pan and to prevent air from being pulled through the drain
To pressurize the drain so water sprays into the return
To store extra refrigerant oil
To increase static pressure in the supply ducts

questions.prompt: A permanent electrical disconnect for an outdoor unit should be located so that:
questions.explanation: A disconnect within sight of the equipment lets a technician isolate power at the unit. Exact code details vary, but the service principle is local, visible isolation.

choices.body: It can be used to isolate power at the equipment during service
It is hidden in a locked closet far from the unit so homeowners cannot find it
It only interrupts the thermostat C wire
It is mounted on the compressor dome

questions.prompt: Where should a room thermostat generally be mounted for a representative reading?
questions.explanation: Mount on an interior wall away from supply blasts, lamps, kitchens, and direct sun so it senses space temperature, not a local false load.

choices.body: On an interior wall away from supply air, lamps, and direct sun
Directly above a supply register
On the furnace vestibule door
On an uninsulated exterior wall in full sun

questions.prompt: A gas furnace needs an adequate supply of combustion air because:
questions.explanation: Burners require oxygen. Starved combustion produces carbon monoxide and poor flame quality. Blocking combustion air is unsafe.

choices.body: Burners need oxygen to burn fuel cleanly and completely
Combustion air cools the compressor
Combustion air is used to dry the evaporator coil
Combustion air replaces the need for a vent

questions.prompt: Why should indoor and outdoor sections of a split system be matched as a designed pair?
questions.explanation: Capacity, metering, airflow, and controls are designed together. Random mismatch can cause poor performance, icing, and compressor damage.

choices.body: Capacity, metering, and airflow are designed to work together
Any indoor coil can be paired with any outdoor unit if the voltages match
Matching only matters for paint color
The indoor section is only a filter box and does not affect capacity

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a Schrader valve core in a service port?
questions.explanation: The core is a spring-loaded check that seals the port until a service hose depresses it. Caps still matter because cores can leak.

choices.body: To seal the service port until a hose depresses the core
To meter refrigerant like a TXV
To ground the suction line
To store oil for the compressor

questions.prompt: Why is the suction line insulated on a typical split air conditioner?
questions.explanation: Suction insulation reduces unwanted heat gain (which adds load) and limits condensation on the cold vapor line.

choices.body: To limit heat gain and condensation on the cold vapor line
To keep liquid refrigerant from freezing in the liquid line
To raise discharge temperature
To make the line set easier to bend

questions.prompt: What is a condensate overflow (float) switch intended to do?
questions.explanation: If the drain backs up, the switch opens the control circuit to stop further condensate production before water damages the structure.

choices.body: Stop the equipment if the drain pan water level rises too high
Increase blower speed when humidity is high
Add water to the pan to keep the trap primed
Bypass the indoor coil when water is present

questions.prompt: Electric heat strips in an air handler are commonly staged because:
questions.explanation: Staging limits inrush current and matches heat output to load. Energizing every kW on a small call wastes energy and can trip breakers.

choices.body: To match heat output to load and limit electrical inrush
To reverse the refrigeration cycle
To dry the liquid-line drier
To start the compressor unloaded

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a crankcase heater on many compressors?
questions.explanation: A crankcase heater keeps refrigerant from migrating into the oil during the off cycle, which helps prevent oil dilution and slugging on start.

choices.body: To keep refrigerant from condensing in the oil during the off cycle
To defrost the indoor coil
To superheat the liquid line
To power the thermostat display

questions.prompt: A hard-start kit is typically added to a single-phase compressor to:
questions.explanation: A start capacitor and potential relay (or PTC) increase starting torque for hard-start conditions. It is not a substitute for correct charge or voltage.

choices.body: Increase starting torque under difficult starting conditions
Raise SEER by lowering running amps permanently
Convert the compressor to three-phase power
Replace a failed run capacitor as a permanent repair

questions.prompt: On a gas furnace, what is the difference between inlet (supply) gas pressure and manifold pressure?
questions.explanation: Inlet pressure is what arrives at the valve. Manifold pressure is the regulated pressure delivered to the burners and must match the appliance rating for the fuel.

choices.body: Inlet is pressure arriving at the valve; manifold is the regulated pressure to the burners
They are always identical, so only one measurement is ever needed
Manifold pressure is the duct static pressure
Inlet pressure is measured at the evaporator coil

questions.prompt: Raising indoor blower speed on a furnace generally does what to temperature rise?
questions.explanation: More airflow across the heat exchanger carries away more heat, so temperature rise falls (within design limits). Too little airflow raises rise and can overheat the exchanger.

choices.body: Temperature rise decreases
Temperature rise always increases
Manifold gas pressure increases automatically
The vent becomes a supply duct

questions.prompt: Why is combustion analysis used on a fuel-fired appliance after setup or major service?
questions.explanation: Combustion analysis verifies that fuel, air, and venting are producing a safe, complete burn (O2/CO2/CO and, where required, temperature/draft). Visual flame color alone can miss dangerous CO.

choices.body: To verify safe, complete combustion rather than relying on flame color alone
To measure refrigerant superheat
To set the thermostat heat anticipator in milliseconds
To calculate duct leakage in CFM25

questions.prompt: A package unit differs from a split system primarily because:
questions.explanation: A package unit contains the evaporator, condenser, and compressor in one outdoor/rooftop cabinet, with duct connections. A split system separates indoor and outdoor sections.

choices.body: The refrigeration and air-handling components are in one cabinet
Package units never use electricity
Split systems cannot provide cooling
Package units have no fans

questions.prompt: On many heat pumps, auxiliary electric heat is used when:
questions.explanation: Auxiliary heat supplements the heat pump in cold weather, during defrost, or when the thermostat calls for emergency/supplemental heat. It is not a refrigerant recovery method.

choices.body: The heat pump cannot meet the load, during defrost, or on an emergency-heat call
The outdoor coil needs extra refrigerant
The compressor is being vacuumed
The condensate pan is dry

questions.prompt: A normally closed condensate float switch is typically wired so that:
questions.explanation: In the control circuit, a closed float allows 24 volts to pass. Rising water opens the switch and interrupts the call. Wiring it to short R to Y would force cooling with a full pan.

choices.body: Rising water opens the control circuit and stops the call
Rising water jumps R to Y to force more cooling
The switch feeds line voltage to the compressor independently of the contactor
The switch closes the gas valve to high fire

questions.prompt: Line-set length and lift matter on a split system because they affect:
questions.explanation: Long lines and lift change pressure drop, oil return, and required charge. Manufacturers specify limits, traps, and extra charge—do not ignore them.

choices.body: Pressure drop, oil return, and required refrigerant charge
Only the thermostat wire color
Only the filter MERV rating
The utility supply voltage

questions.prompt: An induced-draft gas furnace lights briefly, then locks out. The pressure switch is a suspect. What is the most appropriate early check?
questions.explanation: The pressure switch proves the inducer is moving vent products. Check inducer operation, vent/intake obstructions, condensate in the hose, and the hose itself before replacing the gas valve or adding refrigerant.

choices.body: Confirm inducer operation, vent/intake path, and the pressure-switch hose
Replace the indoor TXV because furnace lockout is a refrigerant problem
Jump the pressure switch permanently so the burners can run
Increase manifold pressure well above rating to force a stronger flame

questions.prompt: A condensing (high-efficiency) furnace produces acidic condensate from the secondary heat exchanger. What installation implication follows?
questions.explanation: Condensate is corrosive and must be handled with compatible materials, a proper drain/trap, and protection against freezing or backing up into the furnace. Using ordinary steel pipe or dumping into a furnace vestibule is wrong.

choices.body: Drain materials and routing must be compatible with acidic condensate and must not back up into the appliance
The condensate can be ignored because it is distilled water
The secondary exchanger condensate should be routed into the supply duct for humidity
Acidic condensate should be neutralized by mixing it with refrigerant oil in the pan

questions.prompt: A ductless mini-split indoor unit does not respond, though line voltage is present at the outdoor unit. What should be verified early?
questions.explanation: Mini-splits depend on communication wiring, correct terminal identification, and sometimes a specific interconnect cable. Confirm interconnect wiring and indoor power before replacing the compressor.

choices.body: Interconnect/communication wiring and power at the indoor unit
That the indoor coil has a conventional 24-volt contactor like a packaged RTU
That R-22 has been added regardless of nameplate refrigerant
That the equipment grounding conductor has been lifted to reduce communication noise

questions.prompt: A zoned duct system with a single-speed blower has several zones closed. Supply static is high and the coil is approaching freeze-up. What is a logical system-level concern?
questions.explanation: Closing too many zones without a bypass, variable-speed blower, or dump zone can over-restrict airflow. Do not just add refrigerant. Evaluate zone/bypass strategy and minimum airflow.

choices.body: Airflow may be below the coil’s minimum because too much duct is closed
The compressor needs a larger breaker
The liquid line should be uninsulated to add load
The thermostat C wire should be removed to reduce static

questions.prompt: A TXV sensing bulb must be installed so that it:
questions.explanation: The bulb should contact the suction line with good metal-to-metal contact, correct orientation for line size, and insulation from ambient air. A loose or uninsulated bulb makes the valve unstable.

choices.body: Has good thermal contact on the suction line and is insulated from ambient air
Is left hanging in the airstream so it reads room temperature
Is strapped to the liquid line leaving the condenser
Is mounted on the compressor discharge muffler

categories.name: Troubleshooting & Diagnostics
categories.description: Systematic diagnosis of comfort cooling and heating problems.

questions.prompt: An evaporator coil is frozen and airflow from the registers is weak. What should the technician check early?
questions.explanation: Weak airflow is a leading cause of a frozen evaporator. Check the filter, blower, and duct restrictions before condemning the TXV or adding a large refrigerant charge.

choices.body: Filter, blower operation, and other indoor airflow restrictions
Replace the compressor as the first step
Add refrigerant until the ice melts
Bypass the float switch so the unit can keep running

questions.prompt: A customer reports no cooling. The outdoor unit is silent. What is a reasonable first verification?
questions.explanation: Confirm the thermostat mode/setpoint, disconnect, and breaker before opening the sealed system. Many 'no cool' calls are control or power issues.

choices.body: Thermostat mode/setpoint and whether the unit has electrical power
Recover the entire charge immediately
Replace the indoor coil
Cut the liquid line to see if refrigerant sprays

questions.prompt: Indoor unit is running but there is water on the floor beneath the air handler. What should be checked early?
questions.explanation: Condensate drain, trap, and pan overflow are the common causes. Do not start with a compressor replacement.

choices.body: Condensate drain, trap, and pan overflow path
The outdoor fan capacitor only
The gas manifold pressure
The thermostat heat anticipator

questions.prompt: A furnace does not start. The thermostat is set to heat and the setpoint is above room temperature. What is a logical next observation?
questions.explanation: Confirm a heat call and then watch the ignition sequence (inducer, ignition, proving, blower) rather than replacing random parts.

choices.body: Whether the furnace is receiving a heat call and how far the ignition sequence proceeds
Recover refrigerant from the furnace coil first
Replace the evaporator coil as a first step
Add a hard-start kit to the indoor blower

questions.prompt: The outdoor fan is running and the compressor is running, but the house is not cooling. What measurement helps confirm whether the system is moving heat?
questions.explanation: Supply-to-return air temperature difference (and outdoor operation) shows whether the system is actually cooling. Do not add refrigerant without data.

choices.body: Supply-air to return-air temperature difference
Only the color of the thermostat backlight
Only the age of the air filter printed on the cardboard
The number of fins per inch on the outdoor coil without any temperatures

questions.prompt: A rattling noise started after a storm. What is a safe early inspection?
questions.explanation: Look for debris, loose panels, and fan obstruction with power locked out. Do not reach into a running fan.

choices.body: Lock out power and look for debris, loose panels, or a damaged fan
Reach into the running condenser fan to feel for balance
Add refrigerant to dampen vibration
Bypass the high-pressure switch so the unit ignores the noise

questions.prompt: Ice is forming on the outdoor suction-line service valve during cooling. What is the most appropriate early diagnostic approach?
questions.explanation: Ice on the suction path can come from low airflow, low charge, or a restriction. It does not by itself prove one failed component. Check airflow and then evaluate charge with proper measurements.

choices.body: Evaluate indoor airflow first, then use superheat/subcooling to judge charge or restriction
Replace the compressor immediately because ice always means a failed compressor
Add refrigerant until the ice melts, without measuring the system
Bypass the low-pressure switch so the unit can keep running

questions.prompt: Head pressure is high and the condenser is dirty. What should be done before recovering a large amount of refrigerant?
questions.explanation: Dirty condensers cause high head. Clean the coil and re-evaluate against outdoor conditions before deciding the system is overcharged.

choices.body: Clean the condenser and re-check pressures against outdoor conditions
Recover refrigerant immediately without cleaning
Bypass the high-pressure switch and keep running
Close the liquid service valve to starve the evaporator as a repair

questions.prompt: A compressor hums but does not start. Voltage at the unit is normal. What are appropriate early checks?
questions.explanation: Start/run capacitors and a mechanical lock are common. Check starting components and current/voltage at the compressor before replacing the thermostat.

choices.body: Start/run capacitors and whether the compressor is mechanically or electrically locked
The indoor drain trap primer only
The thermostat backlight setting
The MERV rating sticker color

questions.prompt: A furnace lights, then shuts down after a few seconds. What should the technician observe next?
questions.explanation: Watch whether flame is sensed, whether the inducer/pressure switch stays closed, and whether a limit opens. Cleaning or replacing a flame sensor may be appropriate after confirming the sequence—not jumping safeties.

choices.body: The ignition sequence and which safety or flame-proving step fails
Jump the rollout and limit switches permanently
Disable the inducer so the flame stays in the cabinet
Add refrigerant to the heat exchanger

questions.prompt: A heat pump blows cool air in heating mode except during a brief outdoor steam-off. What is a logical check?
questions.explanation: Cool air during heating can be a defrost event, a reversing-valve issue, or a thermostat O/B configuration problem. Identify whether the unit is in defrost or in the wrong mode before replacing the compressor.

choices.body: Whether the unit is in defrost or the thermostat reversing-valve setup is wrong
Replace the compressor immediately
Remove the outdoor coil so it cannot frost
Charge until the suction line is warm in heating without checking mode

questions.prompt: A contactor chatters on a cooling call. What is a likely electrical cause to check early?
questions.explanation: Chatter is often low control voltage, a loose connection, or a failing coil—not a dirty filter as the first electrical explanation.

choices.body: Low 24-volt supply or a loose control connection at the coil
A dirty return filter as the only electrical cause
A disconnected condensate cap as the only cause
The color of the liquid-line insulation

questions.prompt: The system short-cycles on cooling. What is a sound diagnostic approach?
questions.explanation: Short cycling has many causes: oversized equipment, low airflow, safeties, charge, or control issues. Gather runtime, pressures, airflow, and which device opens—do not immediately replace the compressor.

choices.body: Identify whether a safety, thermostat, airflow problem, or charge issue is ending the cycle
Replace the compressor as the standard first repair
Wedge the contactor closed so it cannot cycle
Remove the low-pressure switch and leave it out

questions.prompt: Suction and head pressures are both lower than expected, and indoor airflow is confirmed. What is a reasonable next evaluation?
questions.explanation: Low-low pressures with good airflow often point toward undercharge or a starved evaporator from a restriction. Use superheat and subcooling together rather than adding a random amount of refrigerant.

choices.body: Compare superheat and subcooling to distinguish undercharge from a restriction
Add refrigerant until the sight glass is meaningless on a TXV system without measurements
Replace the indoor blower capacitor first
Close the return so the coil can get colder

questions.prompt: An ECM blower does not run on a call, though the furnace board shows a request. What should be checked before replacing the blower?
questions.explanation: Harness, control signal, and line voltage at the ECM module are required. Jumping 240 volts onto communication pins can destroy the motor.

choices.body: Line voltage, module harness, and the control command to the motor
Apply 240 volts directly to the communication pins
Add a PSC run capacitor across the ECM leads as a standard repair
Reverse the grounding conductor and a hot leg

questions.prompt: A heat pump outdoor coil ices heavily and defrosts rarely. Outdoor airflow looks blocked by debris. What should happen first?
questions.explanation: Restore outdoor airflow (debris, fan, coil cleanliness) before replacing defrost sensors or adding charge. Blocked airflow causes icing.

choices.body: Clear debris and restore outdoor airflow, then re-evaluate defrost
Disable defrost so the unit stays in heating
Add several pounds of refrigerant to raise outdoor coil temperature
Jump the defrost board to electric heat continuously

questions.prompt: A customer reports intermittent cooling. Connections at the contactor are discolored and loose. What is the appropriate early repair direction?
questions.explanation: Loose, overheated electrical connections cause intermittent operation and are a fire/shock hazard. Repair the electrical issue before a major sealed-system repair.

choices.body: Correct the high-resistance electrical connections and re-test operation
Ignore the connections and recover the charge first
Coat the lugs with refrigerant oil for conductivity
Bypass the contactor with wire nuts as a permanent repair

questions.prompt: After a capacitor replacement, the fan runs but the compressor still will not start. What should be verified?
questions.explanation: A dual capacitor has separate sections. Confirm the HERM (compressor) section rating and wiring, compressor winding conditions, and voltage—do not assume the new part is automatically the correct section or value.

choices.body: That the compressor capacitor section, wiring, and compressor windings/voltage are correct
That the thermostat was set to emergency heat
That the suction line is uninsulated on purpose
That the float switch is jumped for testing permanently

questions.prompt: Cooling is poor. Delta-T is low, and the evaporator is not that cold. Condenser airflow is good. What pair of measurements should be taken next?
questions.explanation: Superheat and subcooling, with airflow already considered, distinguish charge, metering, and compressor problems. Guessing a TXV or adding gas without those readings is poor diagnosis.

choices.body: Superheat and subcooling (with suction and liquid pressures/temperatures)
Only the thermostat model number
Only the filter brand
Only the color of the wire nuts

questions.prompt: Call for cool, 24 volts at the contactor coil, contacts closed, but the compressor is not running. Voltage is present at the compressor terminals. What is the next diagnostic layer?
questions.explanation: Power is reaching the compressor, so evaluate windings, overload, mechanical lock, and start components. Do not add refrigerant as an electrical repair, and do not jump an overload as a permanent fix.

choices.body: Compressor windings, internal overload, and starting components
Add refrigerant to electrically start the motor
Replace the thermostat because Y voltage is already at the coil
Remove the equipment ground to reduce drag

questions.prompt: High superheat and high subcooling are present, condenser is clean, and indoor airflow is good. What is the most consistent sealed-system interpretation?
questions.explanation: Liquid is backing up (high subcooling) while the evaporator is starved (high superheat). That pattern fits a restriction after the condenser, such as a plugged drier or liquid-line restriction—not a simple undercharge.

choices.body: A restriction between the condenser outlet and the metering device
A simple undercharge as the only possibility
A dirty filter as the only possibility
A failed crankcase heater as the only possibility

questions.prompt: A gas furnace rollout switch is tripped. What is the correct service approach?
questions.explanation: Rollout means flame left the heat exchanger/burner area. Find the cause (blockage, cracked exchanger, overfire, venting) before resetting repeatedly. Repeated resets without diagnosis are unsafe.

choices.body: Do not keep resetting it; find why flame left the proper path before returning the furnace to service
Reset it as often as needed so the customer has heat tonight without inspection
Jump the rollout switch and raise manifold pressure
Tape the switch closed and clean the evaporator coil instead

questions.prompt: A system was topped off repeatedly with whatever refrigerant was on the truck. Performance is poor and pressures do not match the nameplate P-T relationship. What should be done?
questions.explanation: A mixed, unknown charge cannot be reliably diagnosed or legally/properly topped off. Recover, determine the correct refrigerant, evacuate, and charge per the manufacturer method.

choices.body: Recover the mixed charge, evacuate, and recharge with the nameplate refrigerant using the correct method
Keep adding the truck refrigerant until pressures look familiar
Vent the mix and run the system empty to dry it
Add oil only, because mixed refrigerants are harmless

questions.prompt: A compressor is noisy and running hot. Suction pressure is high and head pressure is low compared with conditions. Superheat is low. What is a consistent concern to evaluate?
questions.explanation: High suction, low head, and low superheat can indicate weak compression or a mechanical compressor problem, but also measurement error or a reversing valve leaking through on a heat pump. Confirm gauges, valve position, and then compressor performance—do not just add charge.

choices.body: Weak compression or internal leakage (after confirming measurements and valve position)
A simple undercharge as the only explanation
A dirty filter as the only explanation
A failed thermostat battery as the only explanation
